text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A parliamentary commission reveals Iran's support for the outlawed separatist group, the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
- Hungary issues three arrest warrants for Turks suspected of being involved in an attack on Turkey's main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz.
- A Turk living in Hungary, Veysel Ozerdem, says he attacked Yilmaz in a Budapest hotel at the weekend because of the politician's criticism of a gangster.
- President Suleyman Demirel attends the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit in Lisbon.
- Ruling Islamists are planning to change the method for electing the president.
- Washington wants to abolish the U.S.-led air force, Operation Provide Comfort, which protects Iraqi Kurds from a base in Turkey.
- The Islamist-led government takes a step back in plans to sell off teachers' hostels in order to raise money.
- Turkey becomes a Mediterranean heaven for yachts.
- Turkey signs an accord for joint military exercises with Israeli forces.
